old: “My shoulders tightened” and “that wording feels wrong” are different observations. Tightening alone doesn’t explain itself. Ask what happened and whether the invitation fits. An explicit no needs no further justification; change the words, the pace, or the approach. Don’t repeat an unwelcome suggestion more persuasively.
new: There is a big difference between communicating “When you invite people to your house, the back of

shoulders gets really tight” and “That doesn’t feel quite right”. With the latter, if you don’t change something because it doesn’t feel right and it turns out to be a ‘no’, then you need to change something. If something doesn’t work, change something!
